title: Flat road or banked road: which one keeps the car in its lane? Banked holds; flat is off in 1.59 s
description:
Flat road or banked road: which one keeps the car in its lane? The same point car at 50 km/h (13.8889 m/s, the speed held constant: chosen) enters the same curve, lane centre line radius 50 m, in a lane 7 m wide (edges 3.5 m either side of the centre line), on ice with grip 0.1 (chosen); g = 9.807 m/s^2. Holding the curve needs v^2 / R sideways. Top band, the flat road: only the tyres can push sideways and they give at most mu g, so with full-grip steering (the swerve model: the lateral acceleration mu g perpendicular to the velocity) the car follows a circle of radius v^2 / (mu g) and runs wide; after the edge it keeps its full-grip steer off the road (chosen). Bottom band, the road banked at 20 degrees with the outer edge higher: the road's push N tilts toward the centre; per kilogram in the road frame N = g cos theta + (v^2 / R) sin theta and the friction needed along the slope is F = (v^2 / R) cos theta - g sin theta. Both cars are integrated by RK4 at dt = 1e-04 s, the lane-edge crossing located by bisection inside the step and checked against the circle and a half-step rerun. Shown at 1/2 speed, four runs on one clock.

Measured:
- Needed: v^2 / R = 3.858 m/s^2 = 0.3934 g sideways; on the flat road the tyres on ice give 0.1 g, 3.93 times less; the flat road holds this curve only up to sqrt(mu g R) = 25.21 km/h.
- Flat road: the car follows a 196.70 m circle instead of 50 m; it crosses the outer lane edge 3.5 m out after 22.05 m of travel, 1.5876 s after the entry, 25.3 degrees of arc round the curve (closed form on the circle 1.587641 s, small-arc check 21.663 m); at 4 s it is 19.2 m outside the lane centre line, 15.7 m past the edge.
- Banked 20 degrees: the road's push N = 1.0742 weights (9.2156 + 1.3195 = 10.5351 m/s^2 per kilogram; its tilt toward the centre gives 3.6032 m/s^2 of the 3.858 needed); the friction needed is 0.2712 m/s^2 down the slope (inward), a grip of 0.0257 against 0.1 available, 0.0743 to spare; the car stays on its centre line (RK4 offset within 4.1e-13 m).
- The bank alone, with no grip at all, holds sqrt(g R tan theta) = 48.09 km/h; with grip 0.1 the bank holds 40.23 to 55.32 km/h (below it the car slides down the bank, above it up and out).
- Table, the flat car's offset from the lane centre line: 0.5 s 0.3583 m; 1.0 s 1.4180 m; 1.5 s 3.1356 m; 2.0 s 5.4483 m; 3.0 s 11.5627 m; 4.0 s 19.1852 m; the banked car stays at 0 throughout.
- Other speeds on the 20 degree bank with grip 0.1: 30 km/h needs 0.2114 up the slope (slides down the bank), 40 km/h 0.1028 up the slope (slides down, just below the window), 60 km/h 0.1679 down the slope (slides up and out), 70 km/h 0.3179 (slides out); the flat road slides out at all four (needs 0.1416, 0.2518, 0.5665 and 0.7711).
- Other grips on this curve: grip 0.3 holds the flat road up to 43.7 km/h and the bank 19.1 to 68.8 km/h; grip 0.5: 56.4 km/h and 0.0 to 81.9 km/h; grip 0.8: 71.3 km/h and 0.0 to 102.2 km/h.
- The bank that holds 50 km/h on this curve with grip 0.1: 15.76 degrees; with no grip at all 21.47 degrees.
- Checks: RK4 at dt = 1e-04 s against the closed forms, 22 checks, 0 failed; the RK4 crossing agrees with the circle within 1.6e-14 s and the half-step rerun within 1.6e-14 s.

Why: turning needs a sideways push, 0.39 g on this curve at this speed, and on a flat road only the tyres can give it; ice gives 0.1 g, so the car can only follow a 196.70 m circle and runs wide, over the outer edge in 1.59 s. On the banked road the road itself pushes the car: its push is tilted toward the centre and supplies most of the sideways push on its own (3.6032 of the 3.858 m/s^2 needed), so the tyres need a grip of only 0.0257 and the car holds its lane. The bank alone holds 48 km/h with no grip at all.
